finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it. Any authenticated user can set privileged or protected fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, id, email, passwordHash, tenantId, plan) on their own record, causing privilege escalation or account/tenant tampering. The `__proto__` key in JSON.parse output is an own property, and Object.assign uses [[Set]], so it may also set the prototype of req.user, which is a possible prototype tampering vector for that object.
finding.source: req.body (JSON body of PUT /me) from any authenticated user; keys and values fully attacker-controlled
finding.sink: Object.assign(req.user, req.body) followed by req.store.save(req.user), which persists the attacker-chosen fields

trace.note: Route handler for PUT /me receives the request
Object.assign merges all req.body keys into req.user with no allowlist
req.store.save persists the modified user, including any privileged fields
Response returns the full req.user, so any sensitive fields on the user object (e.g. hash) are also exposed

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist, schema validation or denylist in this file. The sibling route /me/profile at users.js:11 does destructure only displayName and bio, which shows the intended restriction and that /me bypasses it. Authentication and body-parser middleware are not in this directory, so I could not confirm them; req.user must be set by upstream auth for the handler to work at all. I could not verify whether req.store.save filters fields.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, and users.js:6 saves it, while the sibling route at users.js:11-12 destructures only displayName and bio. Any authenticated user can therefore set privileged fields on their own record. Auth middleware and the behaviour of req.store.save are outside this directory, but nothing in users.js blocks the write.

verdict_facts.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or schema check and users.js:6 persists the result. Any authenticated user can therefore set arbitrary fields on their own record, and the stricter destructuring in /me/profile (users.js:11) shows /me skips the intended restriction.
